assessment.title: Homework #1 · Operational amplifiers
assessment.instructions: Assume ideal op amps unless a finite open-loop gain or output rails are given. Show your model assumptions, the KCL equations at the op-amp inputs, and a rail (headroom) check. Numeric answers use the units shown.

questions.title: 1) Open-loop saturation
questions.promptHtml:
An op amp has open-loop gain A = 2 × 105 and supply rails ±12 V. With v+ = 1.001 V and v− = 1.000 V, find vo.

  1. Compute the output predicted by the linear model vo = A(v+ − v−).
  2. Compare it with the rails and state the actual output.
hints: There is no feedback path, so the virtual-short assumption does not apply.
A 1 mV differential input times 2×10⁵ is far beyond the rails.
checklist: Clamp to the rail and state the sign.

questions.title: 2) Inverting amplifier: gain and currents
questions.promptHtml:
Ideal inverting amplifier with R1 = 10 kΩ, Rf = 100 kΩ, and vi = 0.15 V. Find vo and the current through R1 and Rf.

Report i1 flowing from vi toward the inverting node and if flowing from the inverting node toward vo.
hints: The noninverting input is grounded, so v₋ ≈ 0 V (virtual ground).
No current enters the op-amp input, so i_f = i₁.
checklist: Write KCL at the inverting node.

questions.title: 3) Inverting amplifier design
questions.promptHtml:
Design an inverting amplifier with gain −20 and input resistance Rin = 5 kΩ. Choose R1 and Rf.

Enter your resistor values into the starting circuit (currently marked ?) to check the design.
hints: For an inverting amplifier the input sees R₁ to virtual ground, so R_in = R₁.
checklist: Solve the gain equation for R_f.
Confirm the sign of the gain.

questions.promptHtml: Ideal inverting summer with Rf = 40 kΩ. Input v1 drives the summing node through R1 = 10 kΩ, and v2 through R2 = 20 kΩ. If v1 = 0.60 V and v2 = −0.20 V, find vo.
hints: The summing node is a virtual ground, so each input current is v_k/R_k independently.
All input currents leave through R_f.

questions.title: 7) Why a voltage follower matters
questions.promptHtml:
A source vs with source resistance Rs = 10 kΩ drives a load RL = 1 kΩ.

  1. Find vL without a buffer.
  2. Find vL with an ideal voltage follower between source and load.

Report each answer as the ratio vL/vs. The workspace draws both cases with vs = 1 V.
hints: Without a buffer, R_s and R_L form a voltage divider.
An ideal follower draws no input current and has zero output resistance.
checklist: Explain why no current flows in R_s in case 2.
